top_choice_rationale: P001 credits one well-defined physical idea, the magic-wavelength lattice in which the trap light shift cancels for the clock transition, to Katori (proposal and first strontium realisations) and Ye (the many-atom regime at 1e-18 and its use for redshift, constants and dark-matter limits). Independent clocks agree below 1e-18, so maturity is settled, and a citation limited to the lattice clock separates it from the 2005 comb and 2012 ion-control prizes. P002 is a genuine prediction followed by decisive experiments, but the pairing mechanism is unsettled, sample variation is large, and a three-name cut leaves out Cao, Fatemi and the hBN moire groups, so I rank it second, above no award.
